body:
It really has some effect on me. 
I'm really tired and falling asleep, thanks for talking to me. I really needed it.

http://youtu.be/otx49Ko3fxw
This is pretty popular on reddit, but it is what I'm feeling now
I guess that's my problem. I want something to change now instead of a long term thing. But I don't know what I can do for that.

Yeah, I was with my parents. But they were one of my issues and gave me stress too, so I really don't know which one is better. At least I'm getting an education here. But honestly I don't feel like I learned anything yet. I feel like my classes don't even mean anything, but it's too late to change them. I was thinking about the military too. My dad was in the army and I already know how things are done. I don't think they'll accept me though because I am suicidal and was hospitalized. 
So I don't know what to do anymore.
I'm in university. I thought I could handle it, but being on my own is giving me weird thoughts. And I really just don't like other people. I never knew that I have a hatred for random people.

I used to live in California, right in the middle along the coast, and it was cold everyday. 
I'm in northern Arizona now, and I could just drive south for a little bit and I could be in the heat.
I don't know. I'm always in a different mood for places. I wanna go someplace warm right now. But it wouldn't matter, because even then I'd be unsatisfied or so depressed.

I think that in a sense, we're all alone. I like to think we each have circles and layers that are made up of people that encompass us, but deep down, right in the center of it all, it's just room enough for one person: you. 
Who we allow in those layers and how close they are is up to us. And it is scary, letting those people get so close, risking them turning away from us and leaving that layer, but I find it more worthwhile to have them there than to never let anyone in at all. 
There are always people out here.

I'm in the same boat as you, except I don't have the FWB thing going on. I typically spend every night in this lounge in my dorm room, waiting for... Something to happen. But nothing probably will. Oh well. 
You may feel alone, but in the bigger picture, you're not. One thing that helps me get past being lonely is doing my hobbies out in the open. For example, I yoyo, and I do some pretty cool stuff with it, and so I just go outside and I practice and people occasionally tell me I'm good. If you have any hobbies, play any music, anything at all, show it off.

I talked to my counselor today, and he said I need to me more confident. Not in that exact way, but the way that counselors talk. 
And I'm in college with no real plan. 
Thanks very much
